newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria negotiates joint gas stock firms.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria negotiates joint gas stock firms.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-owned Bulgargas is negotiating with German firms the establishment of two joint stock firms for trade and transportation of natural gas and gas equipment production, gas officials said on Friday.

They said Bulgargas and Germany's Wintershall AG, which is the energy subsidiary of BASF chemical group, were preparing the establishment of a joint stock company in Sofia for trade, transportation and storage of natural gas and other goods for the energy sector, as well as servicing gas pipelines.
The two firms will have equal shares in the new company, which capital will be 100,000 marks.
The other planned joint stock firm in Sofia will be for the production of gas and industrial equipment.
Bulgargas will hold 34 percent in the venture. Germany's Zimmermann & Jansen GmbH will have a 51 percent stake and another German firm will hold 15 percent. The venture capital will be 100,000 marks.
Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet on Thursday gave a green light to Bulgargas to join the two joint stock firms with German partners, as well as another Bulgarian-Russian venture.
Moscow and Sofia plan to set up a joint venture, named ZAO Inter Trans Investitsii i Torgovli, which will settle part of Bulgaria's payments of Russian gas supplies by barter.
The capital of the venture will be $15,000 and it's headquarters will be in Moscow.
Bulgargas and Russia's Inter Investmarket will hold 40 percent each in the venture. Bulgaria's Biochim Bank and Russia's AKB Stolichnii Bank Sberejenie will hold a 10-percent stake eash.
Bulgaria will receive 3.34 billion cubic metres of Russian gas each year until 2008 under a 20-year intergovernmental agreement and must pay for them in cash.

Bulgaria will receive the remaining 1.2 billion cubic metres of Russian gas under the first 10 years of the agreement by June. These are the last volumes due to Sofia in return for its participation in the construction of Russia's Yambourg field.
